name: comp-467
title: Table With Avatars
description: A four-row account table whose first column holds a circular photo next to a name and handle, followed by email, location, status and a right-aligned balance.
use: A user or team directory needs a photo beside each name inside an ordinary data table.
avoid: The four rows and their remote avatar links are written in the file, so any real data means editing the source.
a11y: Avatars carry the person's name as alt text and headers are real table header cells; there is nothing interactive to focus. (keyboard: n-a, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: On near-black, a five-column table with small grey uppercase headers runs edge to edge. Each name cell starts with a round 40px photo, then a bold name over a faint handle; the balance column sits right-aligned. A small grey caption sits under the table.
behaves: Almost still: as the pointer travels down the rows, whichever row it is over picks up a faint lighter background and the rest stay dark.
customise: People, columns and the caption live in an items array inside the file; changing them is a source edit. Row and header styling comes from the shared table primitives.
weight: light: Four plain table rows and four remote images; no animation code runs.
demo: Four people with emails, cities and balances, captioned "Table with images".
issues: Avatar photos are fetched from GitHub raw URLs, so they stay blank when offline.
The caption "Table with images" is filler text rather than real content.
polishWhy: Tidy spacing and crisp avatars, but plain default table styling and a placeholder caption.
